title: UC Software Carpentry Workshop: Tidy Data
description:
This event is part of the 2026 UC Software Carpentry Fall Workshop Series. All workshops take place from 9:00 am - 12:00 pm. 

  • Sept. 8: Tidy Data
  • Sept. 9: Unix Shell
  • Sept. 10: Version Control with Git
  • Sept. 11: OpenRefine 
  • Sept. 15-16: R (Day 1 and Day 2)
  • Sept. 15-16: Python (Day 1 and Day 2)
  • Sept. 17: SQL
  • Sept. 23: Sharing Research Software (Using GitHub)

For registration information, workshop descriptions, and software requirements, please see the 2026 UC Carpentry workshop page at: https://www.tim-dennis.com/2026-09-08-uc-carpentries/

You will need to register through the link available on the UC Carpentry workshop page (this registration link is managed by UC Santa Barbara this year, but all UC affiliates are eligible to attend). You are welcome to sign up for the entire series or pick the specific workshops that interest you.

Please note that the Python and R workshops take place concurrently as parallel tracks, so you will need to choose between them; all other workshops in the series are available to participants in either track. While most sessions stand alone, please keep the following prerequisites in mind:

  • You should attend both days of the Python or R workshop if you plan to join.

  • The Unix workshop is a strongly recommended prerequisite for the GitHub-based workshops.

title: Exhibition Opening - Past Advocacy, Future Change: HIV/AIDS Campaigns Transforming Dementia Narratives
description:
"If there’s less stigma [around dementia] and people get diagnosed earlier, there could be a movement. So, we need to look to AIDS and HIV, to ACT UP, for the ways they increased visibility that led to something larger."

- Sara Langer, MD, collaborator and former neurologist living with Lewy body dementia

Join us for the opening reception of Past Advocacy, Future Change: HIV/AIDS Campaigns Transforming Dementia Narratives, an exhibition by 2025 UCSF Library Artist in Residence Michelle Memran. Opening during the convergence of World Alzheimer’s Month and Lewy Body Dementia (LBD) Awareness Month, this exhibition invites visitors to consider how lessons from one movement can help reframe another.

The opening reception will take place on the main floor of the UCSF Kalmanovitz Library on the Parnassus Heights campus and will include an introduction to the exhibition, a conversation with the artist, and special guests. 

Past Advocacy, Future Change explores how the bold visual language and community-led messaging of early HIV/AIDS activism can inspire more humanizing, solutions-oriented narratives around Alzheimer's disease and related dementias today. Drawing on archival HIV/AIDS posters, flyers, and activist graphics, the exhibition reimagines these materials within the contemporary dementia landscape. Striking black-and-white imagery is punctuated by selective use of color, serving as a visual metaphor for the gaps, silences, and oversimplified narratives that continue to shape public understanding of changing cognitive abilities. Visitors can also explore a glossary of dementia-related terms and interactive 3D brain visualizations, offering additional context that bridges the science of dementia with its human experience.

The exhibition opening is available to UCSF ID badge holders, and admission is FREE. 

UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in this event because of a disability, please contact Dylan Romero at dylan.romero@ucsf.edu as soon as possible.

title: Bay Area Open Science Group - Evolving approaches to open science and research transparency education
description:
This month we are joined by Jo Weech, Research Transparency Program Manager at the Berkeley Initiative for Transparency in the Social Sciences BITSS. Jo supports teams working on academic forecasting, evidence aggregation, and reporting in economics. In addition to its research projects, BITSS hosts an annual conference and course on research transparency. Her presentation for the September meeting will be on how education in open science and research transparency has evolved due to changes in researcher norms and use of AI.
 
The Bay Area Open Science Group is a growing community for Bay Area academics and researchers interested in incorporating open science into their research, teaching, and learning. Targeting students, faculty, and staff at UCSF, Berkeley, and Stanford, the goal of the community is to increase awareness of and engagement with all things open science, including open access articles, open research data, open source software, and open educational resources. Through this work the group hopes to connect researchers with tools they can use to make the products and process of science more equitable and reproducible.
 

UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in this event because of a disability, please contact Ariel Deardorff at ariel.deardorff@ucsf.edu as soon as possible.

title: Literature Searching in the Age of AI: Where to Begin
description:
Session Overview 

This hands-on workshop focuses on how to best start basic literature searching using a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools.  Discussion will cover questions to consider that guide whether an AI tool, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Consensus, and Perplexity, can be helpful in the literature searching process. Participants will practice searching a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools to critique the results. There will be time for questions and discussion throughout the workshop.

Learning Objectives

  • Determine where AI tools may fit into the literature searching workflow
  • Compare and contrast answers provided by databases vs. AI tools
  • Create prompts to optimize AI tool answers to compliment database searching

Register below to receive the Zoom link and password.

About the series

This session is part of a workshop series called AI in your Toolkit: Critical approaches to using AI in your work.  The next workshop is on Oct. 8 at 11am-12:30pm covering AI Tools for Review Projects.

About the instructor

Josephine Tan, MLIS, is an Education and Research Librarian. She teaches curriculum-integrated literature searching and citation management skills and specializes in medical education research.

Accessibility statement

UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in this event because of a disability, please contact Josephine Tan at josephine.tan@ucsf.edu as soon as possible.

title: Data Analysis with Python and SQL, Part 1
description:
This workshop introduces Python and SQL through a series of common data analysis tasks. Through hands-on programming exercises, participants will learn to import tabular data in CSV and Excel format, specify columns, filter by row value, generate summarizations and descriptive statistics, and create pivot tables. This workshop will also introduce the Google Colab programming environment and strategies for, creating, reviewing, and validating code through Google’s generative AI coding assistant.

NOTE: This event is available to all University of California and California State University affiliates and research partners. Please register using your university email address if you have one. 

This workshop will be offered online through UCSF Zoom and in person at the UCSF FAMRI Library at Mission Bay. All registrants will receive an email from libcal with location information and a Zoom link prior to the start of the workshop. You will have the option to attend in person or online regardless of how you register, so please select the option you think is most likely at the time of registration. 

 

About the series
Data and Document Analysis with Python, SQL, and AI is designed for UCSF researchers and analysts interested in learning Python for Data Analysis, with an emphasis on text analysis and UCSF library collections. Each session will involve short mini lectures, interspersed with hands-on exercises.

For more information on this series, please see the UCSF Library DSOS Github Page at:

https://ucsf-dsos.github.io/UCSF-DSOS-Python-SQL-Workshops

Geoffrey Boushey is a Data Science Specialist at the UCSF Library. Geoff holds undergraduate degrees in Mathematics and English Literature and an M.S. in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research.

title: Using AI in Review Projects
description:
Session Overview 

This workshop will explore different ways in which AI can be incorporated into review workflows, including developing search strategies, grey literature searching, screening, extraction, and writing. We will focus especially on search strategy development using ChatGPT, as well as examine screening tools with varying degrees of automation. This session will also introduce best practices for AI use disclosure and highlight common journal guidelines.

Learning Objectives

  • Assess when AI can effectively be integrated into a review workflow

  • Evaluate AI-assisted search strategies for errors and biases

  • Understand how to disclose AI use in accordance with current recommendations and/or journal guidelines

title: Analyzing COVID Testing Data with Python and SQL
description:
This workshop will teach you how to use SQL and Python to analyze a COVID testing dataset. You’ll begin by using SQL to query and filter data from a database, and then move on to Python for cleaning, manipulating, and visualizing the data. We will also explore how to leverage AI-generated code to streamline and enhance your data analysis workflow. By the end of the session, you'll be able to combine these tools to extract meaningful insights from the dataset.

Note: This workshop will be offered online through UCSF Zoom. You will receive an email from LibCal with room information and Zoom link prior to the start of the workshop. 

Accessibility: UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in this event because of a disability, please contact Geoffrey Boushey by emailing geoffrey.boushey@ucsf.edu as soon as possible.

 

Workshop Series: Data and Document Analysis with Python, SQL, and AI

This series is designed for researchers, staff, and students who want to learn Python from the ground up, focusing on data analysis, document analysis, and AI-based research. Throughout the workshops, we’ll dive into various data types—including numerical data, health data, text, and images/videos—and explore analysis techniques like regression, classification, and sentiment analysis. We’ll put a particular focus on text analysis, especially analyzing documents from our industry document library.

As programming evolves, so does the way we learn it. While we’ll introduce AI-assisted programming earlier in the series than in past workshop series, we’ll still start with the basics. The early workshops (Intro to Python Parts 1 & 2 and Intro to SQL) will use AI sparingly. As the series moves forward, we’ll dive into topics like web APIs, text analysis, natural language processing, machine learning, regression, document analysis, and AI system interaction, with more AI-driven techniques along the way.

For more information on this series, please see the UCSF Library DSOS Github Page at:

https://ucsf-dsos.github.io/UCSF-DSOS-Python-SQL-Workshops
